pass_b_english: And we believe into his name, not believing that he is a common human and one of us, but that he is God become human. And giving authority to become children of God is not a human thing, but rather God-befitting and beyond creation. When therefore the faith is into him, and he himself gives the grace of adoption, how is Christ not God?

“This beginning of the signs Jesus did in Cana of Galilee, and he manifested his glory, and his disciples believed into him.” When the sign had therefore happened, and Christ had manifested his glory, into whom have the blessed disciples believed? Into a holy human simply? And yet even before the sign they followed him, marveling at him as holy. But through the sign they have seen him having power and authority beyond a human. Therefore they have believed as into God. And one must know that many of the saints have done many wonders and were marveled at, yet no one believed into them.

“And when he was in Jerusalem at the Passover in the feast, many believed into his name, seeing his signs that he was doing.” “For God did not send his Son into the world that he might judge the world, but that the world might be saved through him. The one who believes into him is not judged; but the one who does not believe has already been judged, because he has not believed into the name of the only-begotten Son of God.” If the faith into the Son is the way of salvation, how then do we believe into him? Or how will we escape the sentence from being judged? By accepting him as a human and nothing else besides this? Then how will we not worship a human? Or rather as into God? For this is true. Who then will dare to say that he is not truly God, whose faith has justified those under heaven?
